meta.title: Nozawa Onsen Snow Resort
meta.description: ~25 min by bus from Iiyama Station — 100% natural JAPOW and 13 historic soto-yu baths in Japan's iconic onsen snow village.

transit.title:
From Iiyama,
25 min by bus.
transit.lead: ~25 minutes by bus from JR Iiyama Station — step off the slopes into a walkable onsen village. Pair with the Hokuriku Shinkansen for realistic weekend snow-and-bath trips from Tokyo.
transit.imgAlt: Winter bus on snowy road from Iiyama Station toward Nozawa Onsen ski resort

primary.title: Natural powder & forest long runs
primary.lead: One of Japan's deepest snow belts — Yamabiko's ungroomed zones and forest lines up to ~10 km. Nagasaka gondola capacity and season-long premium snow keep core fans coming back.
primary.imgAlt: Skier in deep powder on forest run at Nozawa Onsen

secondary.title: After skiing, 13 soto-yu
secondary.lead: Thirteen communal bathhouses dot the village below the slopes — from Oyu's wooden architecture to coin-donation outdoor baths. An après culture other resorts cannot copy.

onsen.title:
13 soto-yu &
village nights
onsen.lead: Oyu and other 100% spring-fed communal baths, swimsuit-friendly Sparena, and Furusato-no-Yu near Ogama — easy post-ski loops through the onsen town.
onsen.whisper: Soto-yu are cared for by local bath cooperatives. Rinse before soaking and bring a small donation.
onsen.imgAlt: Snow-framed wooden soto-yu bathhouse in Nozawa Onsen village

oyu.title: Nozawa Onsen Oyu (public bath)
oyu.lead: Toyogo, Nozawa Onsen Village. The village symbol — wooden communal bathhouse. Donation-based spring water (verify on site). Tourism association TEL 0269-85-3155.
oyu.imgAlt: Wooden Oyu bathhouse — symbol soto-yu of Nozawa Onsen

sparena.title: Nozawa Onsen Sparena
sparena.lead: Swimsuit large outdoor bath, pool, and sauna — family-friendly day recovery. TEL 0269-85-3166 (resort common line — verify).
sparena.imgAlt: Sparena outdoor bath — large day facility at Nozawa Onsen

furusato.title: Ogama Furusato-no-Yu
furusato.lead: Day-use bath with showers — hot and mild pools plus outdoor bath near Ogama spring. TEL 0269-85-3700 (verify).

nearbyOnsen.pairingLead: Morning: bus from Iiyama → afternoon: Yamabiko powder → evening: LIBUSHI craft beer → night: Oyu and bath hopping → next morning: Ogama viewpoint.

libushi.title: LIBUSHI (Ribushi)
libushi.lead: 9347 Toyogo, Nozawa Onsen. Craft beer brewed with local spring water — standing apéro before Oyu. TEL 080-6930-3992. http://libushi.com/
libushi.imgAlt: Craft beer at LIBUSHI brewery bar in Nozawa Onsen

atarashiya.title: Atarashiya
atarashiya.lead: 8866 Toyogo, Nozawa Onsen. Famous for unagi and yakitori rice bowls — Showa-era atmosphere for classic village dinner. TEL 0269-85-2044 (verify).
atarashiya.imgAlt: Washoku at Atarashiya — legacy Nozawa restaurant

nearbyFood.pairingLead: Morning: bus from Iiyama → midday powder → Sparena soak → LIBUSHI beer → Atarashiya dinner → two soto-yu stops.

powder.title: Natural powder & forest lines
powder.body: 297 ha of skiable terrain — Yamabiko ungroomed zones, self-responsibility areas, and forest runs up to ~10 km. Deep-snow quality in a premier heavy-snow region (verify on official sources).

iiyama.title: ~25 min bus from Iiyama
iiyama.body: ~25 min by bus from JR Iiyama Station — pair with Hokuriku Shinkansen. Rent at Iiyama Station to loop Shiga Kogen, Madarao, and other northern Nagano resorts.

onsen.title: 13-bath village culture
onsen.body: Thirteen communal baths managed by local cooperatives since the Edo period — donation entry and straight-from-source water. Oyu architecture, Ogama village life, and onsen eggs complete the snow-and-culture package.
